static_gk_boosters.title: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India (DFCCIL)
bullets: Established in October 2006 under the Companies Act 1956 as a Special Purpose Vehicle owned by the Ministry of Railways.
Responsible for planning, construction, maintenance, and operation of two major corridors: Eastern DFC (Ludhiana to Dankuni) and Western DFC (Dadri to JNPT).
Headquartered in New Delhi.

static_gk_boosters.title: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)
bullets: Statutory body constituted in March 2007 under the Commission for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act, 2005.
Operates under the administrative control of the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
Ensures all laws, policies, and administrative mechanisms align with child rights perspectives as per the Indian Constitution and UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

static_gk_boosters.title: BRICS & New Development Bank (NDB)
bullets: BRIC term was coined in 2001 by Jim O'Neill; first formal summit held in Yekaterinburg, Russia in 2009.
New Development Bank (NDB) was set up during the 6th BRICS Summit in Fortaleza (2014) with equal voting rights among founding members.
NDB is headquartered in Shanghai, China.

static_gk_boosters.title: National Statistical Office (NSO)
bullets: Formed by merging the Central Statistics Office (CSO) and National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) under MoSPI.
Responsible for publishing key national indicators including Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Index of Industrial Production (IIP), and Consumer Price Index (CPI).
Current base year for GDP calculation in India is 2011-12.

static_gk_boosters.title: Asian Cricket Council (ACC)
bullets: Established in 1983 as the Asian Cricket Conference to foster and develop cricket across the continent.
Headquartered in Colombo, Sri Lanka.
Organizes the biennial Asian Cup tournament for both Men's and Women's national cricket teams.

vocab_words.meaning: To make something bad or unsatisfactory better; to improve.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Digital assessments at RSETIs are designed to ameliorate operational delays in credit disbursement for rural entrepreneurs.

vocab_words.meaning: Equivalent in seriousness, value, or effect to something.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Disregarding regional environmental concerns during ESA notifications is tantamount to ignoring sustainable development principles.

vocab_words.meaning: Intended or likely to placate, pacify, or overcome animosity.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The foreign minister adopted a conciliatory tone to facilitate diplomatic dialogue between the neighboring nations.

vocab_words.meaning: A situation in which no progress is possible; a deadlock or stalemate.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Bilateral trade negotiations reached an impasse over disagreement regarding tariff reductions on agricultural imports.

vocab_words.meaning: Excessive confidence or boldness; audacity.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The chief analyst had the temerity to challenge the central bank's inflation projections during the monetary policy presser.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To remove tension, doubts, or misunderstandings between people by discussing them openly.

idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Prudent monetary intervention by the central bank helped keep runaway retail inflation at bay.

idioms_of_the_day.idiom: Hit the nail on the head
idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To describe precisely what is causing a situation or problem.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: The Governor's speech hit the nail on the head regarding structural weaknesses in supply chain logistics.

static_gk_boosters.title: Kasturirangan Committee on Western Ghats
bullets: Constituted in 2012 as a High-Level Working Group (HLWG) to review the earlier Madhav Gadgil Commission report on the Western Ghats.
Recommended designating approximately 37% (around 60,000 sq km) of the Western Ghats as Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA).
Categorized activities into prohibited (mining, thermal power plants, heavy construction) and regulated categories across six states.

static_gk_boosters.title: Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs)
bullets: Institutional framework established jointly by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), State Governments, and Lead Banks.
Aims to provide short-term skill development training and facilitate credit linkage for rural youth to establish micro-enterprises.
Operates under the umbrella of Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM).

static_gk_boosters.title: Chabahar Port & Strategic Significance
bullets: Located in southeastern Iran in the Gulf of Oman; comprises two main ports: Shahid Kalantari and Shahid Beheshti.
India signed a long-term main contract with Iran's Ports and Maritime Organisation (PMO) through India Ports Global Limited (IPGL).
Serves as the key oceanic port facilitating direct trade bypass around Pakistan into Afghanistan and Central Asia.

static_gk_boosters.title: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
bullets: Established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference; headquartered in Washington, D.C., USA.
Primary objective is ensuring global monetary stability, facilitating international trade, and providing financial assistance via SDR quotas.
Publishes flagship reports including the World Economic Outlook (WEO) and Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR).

static_gk_boosters.title: Freedom of Peaceful Assembly (Article 19(1)(b))
bullets: Guarantees all citizens the fundamental right to assemble peaceably and without arms under Part III of the Constitution.
Subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(3) on grounds of the sovereignty and integrity of India, or public order.
State authorities enforce regulatory measures (e.g., Section 144 of CrPC / Section 163 of BNSS) to regulate designated protest sites.

vocab_words.meaning: Liability to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The sudden spike in crude oil prices increased market volatility across Asian stock exchanges.

vocab_words.meaning: A tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Leaders at the summit called for a reduction in non-tariff barriers to facilitate smoother international trade.

vocab_words.meaning: Something that makes a process or activity happen or happen more quickly.

vocab_words.meaning: Action performed by or affecting only one person, group, or country without the agreement of others.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Unilateral trade sanctions often disrupt international maritime trade routes.

vocab_words.meaning: Clear, logical, and convincing in argument.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: At a point where a crucial decision must be made that will affect the future.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: Under all circumstances, no matter how difficult or challenging.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To reverse the direction of a trend or course of events.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: A course of action or decision that has both positive and negative consequences.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: High commodity prices can benefit resource-exporting nations but act as a double-edged sword by driving local inflation.

static_gk_boosters.title: Foreign Exchange Reserves of India
bullets: Managed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999.
Consists of four components: Foreign Currency Assets (FCA), Gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), and Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) in the IMF.
Foreign Currency Assets (FCA) form the largest portion and are expressed in terms of US dollars, accounting for exchange rate fluctuations of non-US currencies.

static_gk_boosters.title: Strait of Hormuz
bullets: A narrow maritime passage located between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, separating Iran to the north from Oman and the UAE to the south.
Recognized as the world's most critical oil chokepoint, through which approximately 20% to 30% of global petroleum production flows daily.
Crucial for India's energy security, as over 60% of India's crude oil imports originate from West Asian suppliers using this route.

static_gk_boosters.title: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)
bullets: Constituted under Section 45ZB of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, following the 2016 statutory amendment.
Comprises 6 members: the RBI Governor (Ex-officio Chairperson), Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer, and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government.
Operates under a Flexible Inflation Targeting framework, mandated to maintain Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation at 4% with an allowable tolerance band of +/- 2%.

static_gk_boosters.title: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) Measurement in India
bullets: Real GDP measures total economic output at constant base year prices to eliminate inflation effects, whereas Nominal GDP measures output at current market prices.
The current official base year for GDP calculation in India is 2011-12, maintained by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
Gross Value Added (GVA) reflects sector-wise supply dynamics; GDP is derived as GVA plus product taxes minus product subsidies.

static_gk_boosters.title: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) System
bullets: Launched by the Government of India on 1st January 2013 to transfer welfare benefits directly into bank accounts, eliminating intermediaries and leakage.
Powered by the 'JAM Trinity'—Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar unique identity, and Mobile connectivity.
Managed by the DBT Mission, which functions under the Cabinet Secretariat to coordinate implementation across central and state ministries.

vocab_words.meaning: To spread throughout every part of a substance, system, or society.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Inflationary pressures have begun to permeate the manufacturing sector, raising operational costs.

vocab_words.meaning: A confident and forceful statement of fact or belief.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The ministry challenged the company's assertion that the operational delay was purely accidental.

vocab_words.meaning: To make a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling worse.

vocab_words.meaning: To overcome a difficulty, obstacle, or hurdle successfully.

vocab_words.meaning: Regulatory supervision, or an unintentional failure to notice something.

idioms_of_the_day.idiom: To take with a pinch of salt

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To face a difficult situation courageously and take an inevitable tough decision.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: In the process of being planned, developed, or produced.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To reveal confidential or secret information prematurely.

static_gk_boosters.title: Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007
bullets: Enacted to provide for the regulation and supervision of payment systems in India.
Designates the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as the sole authority to regulate payment systems.
Empowers RBI to frame regulations regarding Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) and zero-charge frameworks for digital payments like UPI and RuPay.

static_gk_boosters.title: Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)
bullets: Established in 1963 as Special Service Bureau following the 1962 Indo-China War; renamed Sashastra Seema Bal in 2003.
Functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).
Mandated to guard India's open international borders with Nepal (1,751 km) and Bhutan (699 km).

static_gk_boosters.title: Wholesale Price Index (WPI) vs Consumer Price Index (CPI)
bullets: WPI measures inflation at the producer/wholesale level, published by DPIIT (Base Year: 2011-12) with no services basket.
CPI measures inflation at the retail consumer level, published by NSO (Base Year: 2012) and includes services.
The RBI officially adopted CPI as its primary inflation metric for monetary policy formulation in 2014 based on the Urjit Patel Committee recommendations.

static_gk_boosters.title: Open Court Principle & Article 145 of the Indian Constitution
bullets: Article 145(4) explicitly mandates that no judgment shall be delivered by the Supreme Court save in open court.
Open court justice ensures public transparency, judicial accountability, and public trust in legal proceedings.
Constitutional Bench exceptions exist for in-camera trials under specific statutory provisions like family law or national security.

static_gk_boosters.title: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
bullets: Inserted Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and the 11th Schedule into the Constitution of India.
Gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) creating a 3-tier system: Gram, Intermediate, and District Panchayats.
11th Schedule contains 29 functional items allocated to Panchayats, including education, libraries, and rural infrastructure.

vocab_words.meaning: The act of speaking about someone or something in a derogatory or belittling manner.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The court expressed Chagrin at the disparagement directed toward the independent expert committee before it began its work.

vocab_words.meaning: A state of disuse, inactivity, or neglect.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Several outdated regulatory provisions fell into desuetude following the comprehensive economic reforms.

vocab_words.meaning: Having a subtle, gradual, or highly harmful and destructive effect.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Unregulated cosmetic products containing toxic metals pose a pernicious threat to consumer health.

vocab_words.meaning: An official ban, prohibition, or condemnation of a practice or group.

vocab_words.meaning: A feeling of anxiety, unease, or worry.

idioms_of_the_day.idiom: Burn the candle at both ends
idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To exhaust one's health or resources by working or staying active late at night and early in the morning.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Aspirants preparing for competitive exams often burn the candle at both ends to cover the expansive syllabus.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To discourage, dampen enthusiasm for, or express disapproval of a plan or idea.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Rising inflation numbers threw cold water on market hopes for an early reduction in benchmark interest rates.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: Pursuing a mistaken line of thought, investigation, or course of action.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Focusing solely on supply-side incentives without addressing labor demand means policymakers may be barking up the wrong tree.

static_gk_boosters.title: Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
bullets: Nodal Agency: Statutory body under the Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.
Governing Act: Enforces regulations under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules, 1945.
Key Functionary: Headed by the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI); headquartered in New Delhi.

static_gk_boosters.title: World Trade Organization (WTO)
bullets: Formation: Established on January 1, 1995, as a result of the 1994 Marrakesh Agreement, replacing the 1947 GATT.
Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland; current membership stands at 164 member states.
Highest Body: The Ministerial Conference, which meets biennially to make major decisions regarding multilateral trade agreements.

static_gk_boosters.title: Section 22A of the Registration Act, 1908
bullets: Legal Mandate: Empowers state governments to prohibit registration of documents relating to transfer of public, endowment, or protected lands.
Objective: Prevents fraudulent alienation of government properties and ceiling surplus land.
Constitutional Context: 'Land' and 'Rights in or over land' fall under List II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

static_gk_boosters.title: India-Nepal Energy Cooperation Framework
bullets: Foundational Agreement: Power Exchange Agreement signed between India and Nepal in 1971.
Transmission Asset: The 400 kV Dhalkebar-Muzaffarpur cross-border line acts as the primary transmission artery for high-capacity trade.
Nodal Entities: Grid Controller of India Limited (Grid-India) and Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA).

static_gk_boosters.title: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO)
bullets: Mechanism: Periodic warming of Sea Surface Temperatures (SST) in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
Impact on India: Weakens the pressure gradient required for monsoon winds, frequently resulting in below-normal rainfall in South Asia.
Opposite Phase: La Niña, characterized by cooling SSTs in the Pacific, typically correlates with strong monsoon rainfall in India.

vocab_words.meaning: To render obscure, unclear, or unintelligible, often deliberately.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Complex financial jargon is often used by dishonest firms to obfuscate risk factors from investors.

vocab_words.meaning: To waste money, time, or opportunity in a reckless and foolish manner.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Developing nations cannot afford to squander fiscal resources on non-productive subsidies.

vocab_words.meaning: Not harmful or offensive; harmless in effect.
vocab_words.example_sentence: What appeared to be an innocuous regulatory filing actually triggered a major market reaction.

vocab_words.meaning: Extremely unwilling to spend money or use resources; excessively frugal.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The ministry's parsimonious allocation for capital expenditure slowed infrastructure development.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To successfully survive a difficult period, crisis, or challenge.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To take an action that exacerbates an already volatile or dangerous situation.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Unsubstantiated rumors regarding bank illiquidity only added fuel to the financial panic.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: An event or action that disrupts a planned process or causes a system to malfunction.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Unanticipated tariff policy changes threw a serious spanner in the works of the export consortium.

static_gk_boosters.title: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)
bullets: Established under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952; functions under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
Administered by the Central Board of Trustees (CBT), a tripartite body comprising representatives from Government, Employers, and Employees.
Headquartered in New Delhi; manages three major schemes: EPF Scheme 1952, EPS (Pension Scheme) 1995, and EDLI (Insurance Scheme) 1976.

static_gk_boosters.title: Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) Deposit Scheme - FCNR(B)
bullets: Introduced to allow Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) to maintain term deposits in foreign currencies in India.
Deposits are fully repatriable (both principal and interest), and exchange rate risk is entirely borne by the commercial bank, not the depositor.
Exempt from Indian income tax and wealth tax, serving as an important source of foreign exchange inflow during external current account deficits.

static_gk_boosters.title: Meenakshi Amman Temple & Dravidian Architecture
bullets: Located in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, on the southern banks of the Vaigai River.
Renowned for its towering Gopurams (monumental entrance towers), golden lotus tank (Porthamarai Kulam), and Hall of Thousand Pillars.
Key structural expansions were carried out during the reign of the Nayak Dynasty (notably King Thirumalai Nayak) in the 16th–17th centuries.

static_gk_boosters.title: Outer Space Treaty of 1967
bullets: Formal title: Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies.
Forms the foundational framework of international space law under the auspices of the United Nations Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space (COPUOS).
Explicitly bans placing weapons of mass destruction (WMDs) in orbit, on the Moon, or on any other celestial body, reserving space for peaceful activities.

static_gk_boosters.title: Operation Polo & Article 371(J) (Kalyana-Karnataka)
bullets: Operation Polo was the military action conducted in September 1948 by the Indian Armed Forces to integrate the princely state of Hyderabad into the Union of India.
September 17 is celebrated annually as Liberation Day across the region (Kalyana-Karnataka).

Article 371(J) was added to the Constitution via the 98th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2012, to provide special developmental provisions and reservation quotas for six backward districts of the region.

vocab_words.meaning: Beginning to grow or develop rapidly; flourishing.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The burgeoning digital payments ecosystem has transformed retail trade across rural and urban India.

vocab_words.meaning: Official approval, endorsement, or sanction.
vocab_words.example_sentence: The infrastructure project proceeded smoothly after receiving the official imprimatur of the Union Environment Ministry.

vocab_words.meaning: To reduce the force, intensity, effect, or value of something.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Strategic petroleum reserves are designed to attenuate severe supply disruptions during geopolitical crises.

vocab_words.meaning: Making a hypocritical show of moral superiority or righteousness.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Diplomats criticized the sanctimonious tone of foreign unilateral trade measures imposed without multilateral dialogue.

vocab_words.meaning: Plausible but fallacious or misleading in reasoning.
vocab_words.example_sentence: Economists dismissed the sophistic arguments blaming digital infrastructure fees for broad inflationary trends.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To solve a highly complex or intractable problem in a quick, bold, and decisive manner.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: By introducing direct e-auctions for mineral blocks, the ministry cut the Gordian knot of discretionary natural resource allocations.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To waste energy fighting imaginary enemies or pursuing impractical, unrealistic goals.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Attempting to completely ban commercial digital transactions in a modern economy is merely tilting at windmills.

idioms_of_the_day.meaning: In a state of stagnation, inactivity, low morale, or depression.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: The commercial real estate sector remained in the doldrums until government asset monetization drives injected fresh market liquidity.

idioms_of_the_day.idiom: To keep one's ear to the ground
idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To pay careful attention to upcoming trends, public opinions, and developments.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Central bank policymakers must keep their ear to the ground to anticipate sudden fluctuations in global commodity pricing.

idioms_of_the_day.idiom: To strain at a gnat and swallow a camel
idioms_of_the_day.meaning: To fuss excessively over trivial flaws while overlooking much larger and more serious problems.
idioms_of_the_day.example_sentence: Focusing heavily on minor paperwork errors while ignoring massive systemic audit deficits is straining at a gnat and swallowing a camel.

static_gk_boosters.title: Public Accounts Committee (PAC)
bullets: First set up in 1921 under the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919; currently consists of 22 members (15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha).
Members are elected annually from among Parliament members according to the principle of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
Examines the annual audit reports submitted by the CAG under Article 151 of the Constitution to ensure administrative accountability.

static_gk_boosters.title: National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC)
bullets: Established in March 2022 as a wholly owned Government of India company under the Ministry of Finance.
Initial authorized share capital stands at ₹15,000 crore, with a paid-up share capital of ₹150 crore.
Mandated to undertake monetization of surplus, unused, or underused non-core land and building assets of CPSEs and government agencies.

static_gk_boosters.title: National Quantum Mission (NQM)
bullets: Approved by the Union Cabinet in April 2023 with an outlay of ₹6,003 crore for the period 2023-31.
Nodal Agency: Department of Science & Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology.
Focuses on developing intermediate-scale quantum computers (50-1000 physical qubits) and secure Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) systems.

static_gk_boosters.title: Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP) in India
bullets: Launched in 2003 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) to reduce import dependency and carbon footprint.
Targeted 20% ethanol blending in petrol (E20) moved forward from 2030 to 2025-26 under the updated National Policy on Biofuels.
Ethanol is an ethyl alcohol ($C_2H_5OH$) produced mainly by fermenting sugar derived from sugarcane molasses, corn, broken rice, and damaged food grains.

static_gk_boosters.title: Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)
bullets: MDR is the charge payable by a merchant to the bank accepting card/digital payments to cover transaction handling costs.
The fee is typically split among the issuing bank, acquiring bank, and payment network processor (e.g., NPCI, Visa, Mastercard).
Zero-MDR policy was mandated by the Government from January 1, 2020, for UPI and RuPay debit card transactions to boost digital adoption.
